title: Progress output for long running CLI tasks
when: A command runs for seconds or minutes over many items and the user wants visible progress that does not pollute piped output or CI logs.
prompt:
Goal: A live line on stderr for terminals, sparse plain lines for logs, and silence with --quiet.
Steps:
1. Mode: live when process.stderr.isTTY and process.env.CI is unset; log mode otherwise; off with --quiet or --json.
2. Live: rewrite one line with "\r" + text + "\x1b[K"; redraw at most every 100 ms using a timestamp check, not once per item.
3. Text: "[ 42/180 ] 23% 1.2 MB/s eta 0:41 name.txt", cut to process.stderr.columns.
4. ETA from a moving average of the last 20 item times; "eta ?" for the first items.
5. Unknown total: spinner frames | / - \ plus a running count.
6. Log mode: one line per 10 percent or per 5 seconds, whichever comes later.
7. On finish, error or SIGINT: clear the line, show the cursor again (\x1b[?25h) if hidden, print a summary ("180 files, 3 failed, 41 s").
8. Results still go to stdout, untouched.
Quality bar:
- Progress never appears in a stdout redirect.
- Redraw cost is tiny next to the work.
- The summary always prints.
Pitfalls:
- Redrawing for each of 100000 items, slowing the job.
- A hidden cursor left behind after Ctrl+C.
- Animated frames in CI logs, producing thousands of lines.
Verify:
- [ ] Writes go to stderr.
- [ ] TTY and CI detection present.
- [ ] Redraws throttled.
- [ ] Cleanup on finish and SIGINT.
Output: src/progress.mjs with start, tick and done, used by the main loop.

examples.output: src/progress.mjs: live line on stderr throttled to 100 ms with count, percent and eta, log lines every 10 percent in CI, summary at the end
